configuration: Phantom's own unit-test binary: make SETUP=testkd (build/Makefile_setups) phantomtest, built SYSTEM=gfortran OPENMP=yes, then bin/phantomtest derivshydro on SAB_THREADS=2 threads. run.sh copies only the lines that carry a result (' checking ...', '--> SKIPPING ...', 'PASSED: n of m', 'FAILED: ...', 'TEST SUITE PASSED/FAILED') into OUT_DIR/results.txt, dropping the banner, the host and thread count, the memory report, the timing lines and the randomly chosen epigraph, and it fails the run if no assertion line was printed or if no 'PASSED: n of m' line with n > 0 was printed. The suite reports seven subtests and about seventy assertions.
variant: ic/variant/source.patch raises rhozero, the uniform density the derivatives suites build their test particle distribution from (src/tests/test_derivs.f90:28), by two ulps of binary64: the literal 5.0 becomes 5.0000000000000018, a relative change of about 4.4e-16. The suite's inputs are literals in src/tests/test_derivs.f90, so a unified diff applied to the copy of the tree before the build is the only way to express an initial condition here; ic/nominal/source.patch is empty and ic/<ic>/selectors.txt names the single suite to run. The graded numbers are printed with the es10.3 edit descriptor, four significant digits (src/tests/utils_testsuite.f90:305, :340 and :926), so a two-ulp perturbation is at or below the printed resolution and the two runs are expected to print the same or almost the same text; the bound is therefore set from the printed precision, not from the variant, and is stated as such.
altbuild: the same pinned source built by make SYSTEM=gfortran OPENMP=yes DEBUG=yes (Phantom's own -O0 debug build) with the nominal inputs unchanged: a build a correct candidate could plausibly be, with no change of source or deck

evidence.floor_how: measured by selfcheck on 2026-09-09: run.sh altbuild (make SYSTEM=gfortran OPENMP=yes DEBUG=yes: Phantom's own -O0 debug build of the same pinned source, with the nominal inputs unchanged) against run.sh nominal, graded with the check's own validate.py: all graded values within bound
evidence.calibration: Self-validation on the remote Docker host ale-worker (x86_64, Linux 6.17, 88 cpus, the check run under 16 cpus / 32 GB); the run window and this check's run and build seconds are in comment/pipeline/self-validation.json: 156 graded numbers, spread 3.5e-18; passed.
evidence.fault_argument: How far a wrong port lands is argued from the suite's own hard-coded tolerances, the boundary upstream itself draws between round-off and error: 3.600E-04 on h, 1.000E-03 on divv and curl v, 1.500E-03 on curl v (x), 1.000E-05 on gradh and 2.000E-16 on the mean neighbour count. The tightest physical one is gradh, whose in-code tolerance is 1.000E-05, so a fault in the kernel normalisation or the gradh term has less than that much room before it turns an OK into a FAILED; the native fault probes of the same code path on the evolved checks (the artificial-conductivity switch removed from the Sedov check moves its graded arrays by 1.77e+02; the h-rho iteration tolerance loosened by a factor 100 (tolh 1e-04 -> 1e-02), the smallest plausible convergence fault, moves them by 1.02e-06 on the Kelvin-Helmholtz check and 1.80e-04 on the Sod check) show a real fault landing far beyond that.

warrant: The graded observable is the assertion text bin/phantomtest prints for the 'derivshydro' suite: the same sequence of result lines with the same names and the same verdicts, the same 'PASSED: n of m' summary, and every number on those lines within |candidate - reference| <= 1e-12 + 0.002|reference|. What the check exercises: The upstream unit test of the hydrodynamic derivatives: on a uniform periodic lattice of test particles the suite calls the production derivative path src/main/deriv.F90, which runs the density loop of src/main/densityforce.F90 and the force loop of src/main/force.F90, and compares the result against analytic or independently summed values, printing a max error and the in-code tolerance for each assertion. SETUP=testkd (PERIODIC, IND_TIMESTEPS, CONST_ARTRES) is the build the survey measured as exercising about twice the number of subtests that SETUP=test does for these selectors, because the individual-timestep code paths are compiled in. This selector grades the density sum, the h-rho iteration and its grad-h correction terms, the pressure gradient and du/dt for the adiabatic and isothermal equations of state. The bound is physical because a port that changes the kernel table, the density summation order in a way that is not arithmetic, the h-rho Newton-Raphson tolerance, or the grad-h correction moves the printed max error out of its fourth digit or turns an OK into a FAILED; the in-code tolerances the suite prints for these assertions are 1e-6 and looser, three orders above the printed resolution. It is achievable because the suite writes every error with the es10.3 edit descriptor, four significant digits (src/tests/utils_testsuite.f90:305, :340 and :926), so the smallest difference the graded text can express is one unit in the fourth digit, between 1.0e-04 and 1.0e-03 relative; the relative term is two units of that last printed digit and the absolute term keeps the integer counts on the 'PASSED: n of m' and 'FAILED on n of m' lines exact while allowing the handful of printed errors that are pure round-off, of order 1e-16, to move by their own magnitude. A difference below the printed resolution cannot move the text at all, which is why this check's floor is exact or near-exact agreement rather than a small number: the two runs printed the same 156 graded numbers to within 1.34e-17 in absolute value, the only movement being in the printed errors that are pure round-off. Calibration: the shipped self-validation record, comment/pipeline/self-validation.json, is the authority for the run window, for the per-check run and build seconds and for the suite totals, and this file quotes none of them; the record scored reward 1.0 with 13 of 13 checks passed, inside the 900 s guidance budget, which counts run time and excludes the source builds. This check graded 156 numbers with a spread of 3.5e-18. The bound is left as authored and confirmed by the record: rtol 0.002 is two units of the last digit the es10.3 edit descriptor prints, which is what grades every number that carries physics, and atol 1e-12 is the floor that keeps the printed values which are pure round-off from being graded at their own magnitude. The round-off-magnitude value this suite prints is the curl v (y) residual, graded by upstream against an in-code tolerance of 1.000E-03: the quantity is analytically zero and carries no physics, so a legitimate port may move the residual by its own magnitude, and atol 1e-12 sits orders above it and orders below upstream's tolerance. The measured spread, 3.5e-18 in the container and 1.34e-17 natively, is exactly that residual shifting in its last digits, so the review table's margin of 2.9e+05 is the ratio of the bound to a round-off residual's movement, not to the graded precision; a tighter atol (1e-14 would still sit 61 times above the residual) is available to the curator at the cost of a false-failure risk on a port whose round-off differs more. On the lines whose in-code tolerance is tighter than atol - the near-exactness assertions - it is not the numeric bound that grades but the assertion verdict: validate.py requires the same line skeleton, the same OK/FAILED token and the same 'PASSED: n of m' counts, so any change that crosses upstream's own tolerance fails the check whatever atol is. How far a wrong port lands is argued from the suite's own hard-coded tolerances, the boundary upstream itself draws between round-off and error: 3.600E-04 on h, 1.000E-03 on divv and curl v, 1.500E-03 on curl v (x), 1.000E-05 on gradh and 2.000E-16 on the mean neighbour count. The tightest physical one is gradh, whose in-code tolerance is 1.000E-05, so a fault in the kernel normalisation or the gradh term has less than that much room before it turns an OK into a FAILED; the native fault probes of the same code path on the evolved checks (the artificial-conductivity switch removed from the Sedov check moves its graded arrays by 1.77e+02; the h-rho iteration tolerance loosened by a factor 100 (tolh 1e-04 -> 1e-02), the smallest plausible convergence fault, moves them by 1.02e-06 on the Kelvin-Helmholtz check and 1.80e-04 on the Sod check) show a real fault landing far beyond that. If a later run shows the printed digits moving further, the right response is to state the measured spread, not to widen the bound by hand.

official_test.note: run as the upstream harness runs it: make SETUP=testkd phantomtest; ./bin/phantomtest derivshydro

graded_window.note: the whole upstream suite for this selector; nothing is shortened, and the suite is one upstream procedure that cannot be subdivided. SAB_SELECTORS can name a different selector for iteration, but a selector that matches nothing makes phantomtest fall through to the entire test suite

observable: the 156 numbers and every assertion verdict on the result lines bin/phantomtest prints for the derivshydro suite, plus the SKIPPING lines and the PASSED n of m summary
